fatal_errors: The proposed Fe-Cr-Ni-Co-Mo HEA does not reconstruct the tested AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA or its L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The stated 500 °C condition is incompatible with the immersed deionized-water tests conducted at 25–100 °C and risks implying continuous high-temperature service that was not studied.
The mechanism centers on grain-boundary segregation and lattice distortion rather than passive-film repair, tribo-layer stability, depassivation, and the retained dual-phase microstructure.
The baseline is changed from identically tested duplex stainless steel 2205 to an unspecified traditional alloy or 316L.
The claimed 30% wear and 25% corrosion reductions are unsupported inventions and miss the observed approximately order-of-magnitude wear-rate advantage.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad question—whether an HEA can outperform conventional structural alloys under combined thermal and tribo-corrosive exposure—and proposes a testable comparison. However, it does not identify the relevant material, microstructure, comparator, aqueous temperature range, or temperature-dependent wear minimum near 50 °C. Its proposed mechanism is largely unrelated to the demonstrated competition between depassivation, repassivation, abrasion, and tribo-layer disruption. Although its falsification experiment includes quantitative wear and corrosion measurements and a comparator, the conditions are underspecified and mismatched, while the numerical performance claims have no evidentiary basis.
